title: Muhurat Trading 2026: Date, Time, Meaning and Trading Tips
summary: Check the confirmed Muhurat Trading 2026 date, NSE and BSE timing updates, session rules, available segments and practical Diwali trading tips.
body_markdown:
**Muhurat Trading 2026 will take place on Sunday, November 8, 2026, for Diwali Laxmi Pujan.** Both NSE and BSE have confirmed the date, but the exact session timings have not yet been announced.


Muhurat trading is a special stock market session conducted on Diwali. It holds cultural significance for many investors and traders who view the session as an auspicious time to begin the new Samvat year.


However, the market follows normal trading principles during this session. Festive sentiment does not guarantee positive returns, and every trade still carries market, liquidity and execution risk.

## What Is Muhurat Trading?


Muhurat trading is a special trading session held by Indian stock exchanges on Diwali. The word “Muhurat” refers to an auspicious period selected for beginning an important activity.


Many investors use the session to make a symbolic investment, begin a new portfolio or perform a traditional token trade. Brokers, exchanges and financial institutions also mark the occasion with Diwali ceremonies.


Although it takes place outside the normal market schedule, orders placed during Muhurat trading are real. Profits, losses, brokerage, taxes and settlement obligations apply as they would during a regular trading session.


## Why Is Muhurat Trading Conducted?


Muhurat trading combines an Indian cultural tradition with participation in the securities market.


Diwali is associated with prosperity, new beginnings and the worship of Goddess Lakshmi. For many trading and business communities, the occasion also marks the beginning of a new Samvat year.


This is not the beginning of India’s financial year, which starts on April 1. The Samvat year is a traditional calendar followed by several communities.


The session continues as a market tradition on both NSE and BSE, allowing investors and traders to participate in the market during the auspicious period.


## How Does Muhurat Trading Work?


Muhurat trading is shorter than a regular trading day. The exchanges publish a circular specifying the exact schedule and the market segments that will be available.


The schedule may include:


-


Block deal session


-


Pre-open session


-


Normal market session


-


Call auction session for applicable securities


-


Closing session


-


Trade modification cut-off


The order of these sessions and their timings can change each year. Refer to the official 2026 circular once it is released.


During the normal Muhurat market session, participants can place permitted market and limit orders through their brokers. Exchange rules, price bands and risk-management requirements continue to apply.


## Which Markets Are Open During Muhurat Trading?


The segments available for Muhurat trading are specified in the annual NSE, BSE and commodity-exchange circulars.


Depending on the exchange announcement, these may include:


-


Equity


-


Equity derivatives


-


Securities lending and borrowing


-


Currency derivatives


-


Commodity derivatives


Do not assume that every segment will follow the same schedule. NSE, BSE and commodity exchanges may issue separate circulars with different timings and trading instructions.


If you plan to trade futures or options during the session, first understand the[difference between futures and options](https://algotest.in/blog/difference-between-futures-vs-options/) , including their margin, premium and risk characteristics.


## Is the Stock Market Closed on Diwali 2026?


November 8, 2026, is a Sunday and is listed as a Diwali Laxmi Pujan trading holiday. Normal market hours will not apply.


However, NSE and BSE will open for the special Muhurat trading session at the timings announced in their circulars.


This means the market is closed for the regular session but opens for a limited special session.


## Can You Trade Normally During Muhurat Trading?


Orders placed during the permitted Muhurat session are genuine exchange orders. They can result in actual holdings, open derivative positions, profits or losses.


However, trading conditions may differ from an ordinary session because:


-


The session is much shorter


-


Participation may be uneven across securities


-


Bid-ask spreads may be wider


-


Some stocks or contracts may have limited liquidity


-


Festive sentiment can influence activity


-


Sudden price movements may leave less time to react


Broker services may also follow special schedules. Check when your broker will accept orders, provide margin reports and[square off](https://algotest.in/blog/what-is-square-off-in-trading) applicable intraday positions.


## Does the Market Always Rise During Muhurat Trading?


No. Muhurat trading does not guarantee that the Sensex, Nifty or individual stocks will close higher.


Festive optimism may support sentiment, but the market can still react to:


-


Global market movements


-


Company announcements


-


Institutional activity


-


Economic data


-


Commodity and currency changes


-


Geopolitical developments


-


Profit booking


Historical performance cannot reliably predict the result of the next Muhurat session. Avoid buying a security solely because the session is considered auspicious.


## How to Prepare for Muhurat Trading 2026


Because the trading window is limited, prepare your plan before the session begins.


### 1. Confirm the Official Timings


Check the latest NSE, BSE and broker announcements. Old Muhurat trading schedules should not be used because the timing changes every year.


### 2. Create a Watchlist in Advance


Research the securities you want to monitor before Diwali. Avoid selecting stocks only because they are trending on social media during the session.


Your watchlist may consider:


-


Liquidity


-


Bid-ask spread


-


Company fundamentals


-


Recent announcements


-


Valuation


-


Price volatility


-


Your investment or trading objective


### 3. Check Your Trading Account


Log in before the pre-open session and confirm that:


-


Your[broker](https://algotest.in/blog/best-brokers-for-algo-trading-in-india) connection is active


-


Required funds or margin are available


-


Your demat and trading account is functional


-


The selected segment is enabled


-


You understand the broker’s special-session policies


### 4. Decide Between Investment and Trading


A symbolic long-term purchase and a short-term Muhurat trade have different objectives.


If you are investing, assess the business and valuation rather than focusing on the movement during a one-hour session.


If you are trading, define your entry, exit, stop-loss and position size in advance. Our guide to the[best intraday trading strategies](https://algotest.in/blog/best-intraday-trading-strategies-rules-tips/) explains how to create objective trading rules.


### 5. Consider Using Limit Orders


Liquidity can vary during the shortened session. A market order may execute at a price different from the one visible when the order was placed.


A limit order lets you specify the highest price you are prepared to pay or the lowest price you are prepared to accept. However, it may remain unfilled if the market does not reach your limit.


### 6. Keep the Position Size Controlled


Festive sentiment should not change your normal risk limit. Do not increase your trade size simply because you expect the session to be positive.


### 7. Avoid Unverified Stock Tips


Diwali often brings lists of “Muhurat picks” and assured-return messages. Verify the source and conduct your own research.


Guaranteed or assured stock market returns are a major warning sign.


## Muhurat Trading Tips for Investors


Muhurat trading is often treated as a symbolic investment occasion. If you plan to participate as an investor:


-


Start with your existing financial plan.


-


Choose a security only after researching it.


-


Consider portfolio diversification.


-


Avoid concentrating money in one stock or sector.


-


Do not confuse a low share price with a cheap valuation.


-


Think beyond the movement during the special session.


-


Review costs and taxes before placing the order.


The long-term performance of an investment depends on the underlying business and the price paid, not the occasion on which it was purchased.


## Muhurat Trading Tips for Active Traders


A shorter session can make intraday execution more difficult. Active traders should consider:


-


Trading only liquid instruments


-


Watching the bid-ask spread


-


Avoiding oversized positions


-


Using predefined stop-loss rules


-


Accounting for brokerage and slippage


-


Avoiding trades driven only by festive optimism


-


Checking the broker’s square-off time


-


Closing positions according to the original plan


A strategy tested during normal sessions may behave differently during Muhurat trading because the available time, liquidity and participant behaviour can change.


## Should You Backtest a Muhurat Trading Strategy?


A single Muhurat trading session does not provide enough data to judge a strategy on its own. Since the session occurs only once a year and follows a shorter schedule, backtesting only Muhurat sessions can lead to unreliable conclusions.


Instead, test the strategy across a broader range of market conditions. For example, if you plan to trade a breakout during Muhurat trading, evaluate the same rules across regular sessions with different volatility, liquidity and trend conditions.


You should also review:


-


Entry and exit accuracy


-


Average profit and loss


-


Maximum drawdown


-


Slippage and brokerage costs


-


Performance during volatile sessions


-


The impact of limited trading hours


After[backtesting,](https://algotest.in/blog/why-do-we-need-backtesting) use[paper trading](https://algotest.in/blog/paper-trading-vs-live-trading) to practise order placement and risk management without putting real capital at risk. This can help you identify execution issues before the live session.


A strategy that performs well during normal market hours may not behave the same way during Muhurat trading because of shorter trading windows, uneven liquidity and festive market sentiment.


## Common Muhurat Trading Mistakes


### Assuming the Market Must Rise


Cultural significance does not remove market risk. Prices can move in either direction.


### Copying Last Year’s Timings


The exchanges publish a new schedule every year. Verify the 2026 circular before the session.


### Buying Without Research


A symbolic purchase is still an actual investment. Poor-quality stocks do not become better investments because they are purchased on Diwali.


### Ignoring Liquidity


A short session may have uneven liquidity. Check the order book and spread before trading.


### Taking Excessive Risk


Do not increase leverage or position size because the session feels special.


### Following Social-Media Tips


Avoid acting on anonymous stock calls, guaranteed-return messages or urgent recommendations without proper research.


## Conclusion


Muhurat Trading 2026 will be conducted on **Sunday, November 8, 2026** , on NSE and BSE. The exchanges have confirmed the date, while the exact session timings are still awaited.


The session is an important market tradition, but normal principles of research and risk management still apply. Confirm the official timings, prepare your watchlist and avoid treating festive optimism as a trading signal.
